title: impact-scan:v1 structured output block
description: Machine-readable form of the fenced ```impact-scan:v1 code block that skills/pre-implementation-impact-scan/SKILL.md's 'Structured output block (impact-scan:v1)' section (that section is the normative spec; this schema is its machine-readable mirror) requires at the end of an impact-scan report -- exactly one such block per report. Two design principles this schema enforces structurally, both explained in that section: (1) raw observations only, no synthesized aggregate score/rank/priority field -- the scan reports what it found, and leaves 'is this impact large or small' to the downstream consumer; (2) no `digest` field -- a consumer that needs a reproducibility digest computes it itself from candidate_paths+candidate_layers, so a stale or hand-edited digest can never silently pass through this block (see lane's ImpactScanSnapshot: its `digest` field is added AFTER parsing this block, by the consumer, and is never accepted from the block itself).

repo_commit.description: sol architect-review 2nd round must C, nit-fixed 3rd round: full hash only -- either the 40-hex full-SHA-1 form or the 64-hex full-SHA-256 form (40 hex chars IS the full length of a SHA-1 hash, not an abbreviated/short one -- an earlier draft's comment miscalled it "short-SHA1-length," backwards terminology this fixes). A 7-character abbreviated commit (git's default short form) is no longer accepted; abbreviations are ambiguous across a growing repo in a way a reproducibility-critical field like this one cannot afford.

candidate_paths.description: No duplicates (uniqueItems, schema-enforced) -- the skill's own example has no duplicates, so this isn't a contradiction of the normative spec. Sort order is deliberately NOT a wire requirement (sol architect-review 2nd round must C, main裁定): skills/pre-implementation-impact-scan/SKILL.md's own literal example (['src/foo/Bar.ts', 'src/foo/Bar.test.ts']) is not sorted ascending, so requiring sort here would contradict the normative spec this schema mirrors. A CONSUMER that needs a reproducibility digest MUST sort (and dedup) candidate_paths+candidate_layers itself before hashing them, so two equivalent scans discovered in different orders still produce the same digest input -- that responsibility lives on the consumer side, not the wire format.

candidate_layers.description: Same uniqueItems rule as candidate_paths, and the same consumer-side sort/dedup-before-digest rule -- sort is not a wire requirement here either.
